s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging breast swelling with signs of inflammation and skin involvement
salient_findings: Tender swelling in the outer half of the right breast
Overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction
Skin fistula with pus extruding and orange peel appearance of the skin
key_facts: 42-year-old woman
3-month history of gradually enlarging right breast swelling
No history of tuberculosis or tuberculous contact
No family history of cancer
Five children
Using a contraceptive device for 5 years
Tender swelling in the outer half of the right breast
Overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction
Mobile ipsilateral axillary lymph node measured 2.5 cm
No nipple discharge
Infectious workup was strictly normal
Ultrasonography and mammography showed an ACR-4 lesion
Empirical fluoroquinolone was started
Skin fistula developed with pus extruding after 7 days
Breast MRI revealed multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly enlarging breast swelling with signs of inflammation and skin involvement

shortlist.label: Granulomatous mastitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls and skin fistula

shortlist.label: Breast abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Development of skin fistula with pus extruding and overlying warmth, erythema

shortlist.label: Mastitis
shortlist.why_kept: Tender swelling, overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction

shortlist.label: Idiopathic granulomatous mastitis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to granulomatous mastitis, with multiple lesions and skin involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a rapidly enlarging breast mass, overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction, along with the development of a skin fistula and the imaging findings of multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls, is most consistent with inflammatory breast cancer, which is a highly aggressive and rare form of breast cancer.

rejected.label: Granulomatous mastitis
rejected.why: While granulomatous mastitis can present with similar symptoms, the lack of systemic symptoms and the specific imaging findings make it less likely.

rejected.label: Breast abscess
rejected.why: The presence of multiple lesions and the development of a skin fistula are not typical of a simple breast abscess.

rejected.label: Mastitis
rejected.why: Mastitis typically presents with more localized symptoms and does not usually progress to the formation of multiple lesions or a skin fistula.

rejected.label: Idiopathic granulomatous mastitis
rejected.why: This condition can present with similar symptoms, but the imaging findings and the rapid progression of the disease are more consistent with inflammatory breast cancer.
